description: Interactive step-based cryptarithm solver for Grade 7 Mathematics — Chapter 6: Number Play. Displays cryptarithm puzzles in vertical addition format with letter placeholders. Six progressive phases covering two puzzles: T+T+T=UT (simple, single-column) and K2+K2=HMM (multi-column with carry). Active column highlighted with a glowing border. Digit testing shown as a scrolling list where invalid digits are crossed out in red and the valid digit glows green. Carry values shown as small superscript numbers between columns. Solved letters appear in a decoder panel on the side with letter-to-digit mappings. Emerald green accent (#10b981) for solved digits, red for eliminated digits, amber for active testing. Vertical addition layout with clear column separators. Indian school context — described as detective work decoding secret messages. Clean educational design with Lilita One font family and Space Mono for decoded digits. Touch-friendly, mobile-responsive. 5-colour palette: emerald, red, amber, white, dark grey.

instructions_for_student: Follow along as we solve two cryptarithm puzzles step by step. Watch how we work column by column from right to left, testing digits systematically and tracking carries. After the guided examples, try the practice puzzles on your own!

teaching_notes.step_1: Build excitement — frame it as code-breaking. You are a detective decoding secret messages!
teaching_notes.step_2: Let the student guess before systematic testing. Ask: What do you think T could be?
teaching_notes.step_3: Emphasize testing ALL digits 0-9, not just guessing. This is the systematic approach.
teaching_notes.steps_4_to_6: Introduce the column-by-column strategy and carry handling — just like regular addition.
teaching_notes.step_8: Point out the leading-zero trap (K=2 gives H=0) — this is a very common mistake!
teaching_notes.after_tool: Give students the practice cryptarithms (YY+Z=ZOO, B5+3D=ED5, KP+KP=PRR, C1+C=1FF) to solve independently.
